gate:
A handshake wants to happen. Underneath the warmth of liking someone, there is a quieter pull toward agreement, toward the small contract that turns affection into a bond two people can actually rely on. This is that pull. It carries the loyalty that holds a small circle together over time, the emotional charge of friendship and family, the felt insistence that giving and getting should balance out and that promises should land where they were aimed.

Most people misread it as softness, a sweet sociability that loves to please. What moves underneath is closer to a quiet accounting. Who showed up. Who fed whom. Who slipped away when it mattered. Break the bargain and this drive does not stay polite. It tracks. It remembers. The friendliness in it is real, and so is the cost of betraying it. A person carrying this is built for bonds with teeth in them, kindness that keeps a ledger.
centre_field:
This drive is wired to the part of you that runs on feeling, the slow weather that fills a room before anyone has spoken. That is the whole teaching. Friendship here is not a thought about other people. It is a chemistry, a wave that rises and falls inside you, a mood that builds and breaks on its own schedule. The desire to belong sits inside the same circuitry that produces passion, hope, sweetness, and the slow accumulation of resentment when an agreement quietly goes unhonoured.

Because the wave is tribal in flavour, the buildup is polite. Things get stuffed, smoothed over, kept civil. Then a small broken promise lands and the whole pressure releases at once, an outburst that surprises everyone in the room, the speaker most of all. This is why the bond cannot stay only sweet. The feeling has its own clock, and the clock keeps time whether you watch it or not.
channel:
Friendship needs somewhere to land. On its own, this code is all reach, all the warmth of the bargain offered up and waiting for a counterpart. What it reaches for is a different strength in a person, the willed kind that has learned to stand alone before it agrees to belong. The lineage calls the joining of these two community.

The pairing matters. Belonging that has not first known solitude collapses into enmeshment, a constant friendliness with no spine underneath. The aloneness gives the bond a backbone, the will that can say a clean yes and a clean no, the strength to actually deliver on what was agreed. Without that other half, this code keeps making promises it cannot quite carry, drawing people close and then resenting the weight of them. Joined, the bargain becomes a community, and the community can actually hold the members it gathered.
